_comment: Retired model -> its replacement, for scripts/migrate-agent-models.js.
Each entry carries BOTH the target model and the target provider. The
provider is spelled out per row rather than derived in code so that a human
reviewing the dry-run output can audit every line without reading the
script. It is also genuinely necessary: the GPT-5.6 models cannot be served
by the built-in `openAI` provider at all, so those agents change provider as
well as model.
The provider string must match either a built-in LibreChat endpoint name or
an `endpoints.custom[].name` in librechat.yaml, BYTE FOR BYTE, spaces
included. A mismatch fails at request time, not at startup, so nothing warns
you. .github/workflows/validate.yml asserts this on every pull request.
Mapping rule: each retired model maps to its SAME-TIER successor. Never map
down to save money and never map up to be generous — either is a change the
agent's author did not ask for and did not consent to.
Signed off by John on 2026-07-29.
2026-07-30: the last three rows were added after the first dry run against
real data refused to proceed. They appear ONLY inside agents' versions[]
snapshots and never as a live top-level model, which is why the §3.3 survey —
which counted top-level models only — did not find them. gpt-5-nano and
gpt-4.1-mini are the same two drift bugs §11.2 flagged in titleModel and
memory.agent.model, captured into agent history.
Note that gpt-5.1 maps to luna rather than to terra, where the other
plain-numbered models go. Specified by John on 2026-07-30; recorded here
because it is a deliberate exception to the same-tier rule above, and a
future reader comparing the rows would otherwise read it as a mistake.
